- $P(x, y)$: A single-precision floating-point number [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes the approximation method using Schraudolph's technique, where $I(P)$ is a 32-bit integer constructed to approximate the 'IEEE 754 single-precision representation' of the exponential. The formula for $I(P)$ involves scaling $P$ by $2^{23}$ and adding a bias term, which are operations performed on the bit-level representation of a single-precision float. Furthermore, the text refers to 'reinterpret_float' to get the result, implying $P$ is treated within the context of single-precision floating-point arithmetic and representation. The variable $P(x,y)$ itself is a computed value (sum of polynomial terms and log opacity) which is then used in this single-precision bit-level approximation scheme. Thus, the context supports that $P(x,y)$ is handled as a single-precision floating-point number in this specific optimization context.
